sections.text: What is action and what is inaction? It is a question which has bewildered the wise. But I will declare unto thee the philosophy of action, and knowing it, thou shalt be free from evil.
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।
It is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, for mysterious is the law of action.
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
He who can see inaction in action, and action in inaction, is the wisest among men. He is a saint, even though he still acts.

So we had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Renouncing Actions in Knowledge. Its all about knowledge. Its all about Karma.
So the first thing we have seen in this chapter is where Bhagavan gave his identity: my nature is that Im unborn. And because his nature is Ajaha, the nature of myself is also Ajaha -- unborn. But as long as I am in this life, that will continue performing actions.
So also I need to understand actions. Bhagavan said that this world is created by me and it is regulated by Dharma. It is regulated by the laws of nature that we know.
The laws of nature have no exceptions and therefore theyre self regulated. Nobody has to vouch over law of gravitation. Nobody vouch over the laws of thermodynamics.
And you can rely on them. Only time the people deviate from the Dharma is when they have free will. The human beings are the only one who have free will.
So when they deviate from that Dharma, Bhagavan said, I manifest to make that Dharma aligned again. So we can say at the micro level, when I will deviate from my Dharma, the situation will teach me to come back to my Dharma. You learn a lesson by your own actions, by your own situations.
And then as long as there are good thoughts, as we have seen, it says Paritranaya Sadhunam Vinasaacha Duskrita. At the macro level, you can say the whole human society in micro level, when there are good thoughts, are overwhelmed by the bad thoughts in my mind. But one thing, as long as you hang on to the good thoughts, I will manifest in your mind and take care of all the bad thoughts so that the good thoughts will thrive and then you will be able to do what is right for you.
Well, then the question obviously occurred: why cant everyone understand what is right and wrong? Bhagavan said, because in this world it is easier for us to find the results of our actions, so we pursue our senses and pursue the deities of our senses. In other words, we try to get success out of our actions. And thats miserable and enjoyable.
I can see that I have done something and I got these results. So then we get more and more attached to those actions. Thats where the problem starts.
So the whole chapter is all about how to detach yourself from your own actions. Therefore he said that this yoga I have taught to Vivaswan. And then he taught to Manu and the Manu taught to Eswaku.
And thus all those Rajasis knew what is right, how to act in this world. So you are liberated. So youre not bound by your actions.
But over a period of time that is lost. So people are all got then attached to the actions. Everybody is trying to put more importance in what I have accomplished and achieved.
And thats how you are judged by the society, by yourself. And they say thats what the problem is. So Im teaching you this yoga which will liberate you from that.
And then he said, obviously all people are not made equal. Chatharuvanyam Maya Guna Karma, vi Pagisah that in any given society the people are four types. And as we discussed last time, no matter how hard you try, you will not be able to justify that.
Bhagavan meant the four caste system universified. There are not four types of colors, Chatruvand. Four types of people of different colors I have created.
So these were about the skin colors. Obviously there are no four types of skin colors in our society. Or you can look at it this way.
The colors are associated with Satvaraja and Tamas as white, red and black. And then they have added the yellow as the Vaishya. Then its one of the commentary I have read says, okay, if thats the case, if it was a skin color, all whites are Brahmins, all red Indians are Kshatriyas, all Mongolis.
People who are yellowish are Vaishyas and all dark people are Shudras. Thats not true either. So these are the colors of your mind.
These are the colors of ones mental textures. See, the people in this world come with four different mental textures. And depending on the Guna and karma, they are divided into the four classification.
Any given society at any given time that I am the author of them. In other words, they exist because of me. But Im not involved in.
I didnt create them. They are by themselves have their own gunas and karmas. So even though I Act, I do not participate in that.
As this self, as the supreme Self, there is no creation. All exists is himself as one single entity. And therefore what is created is in perception only.
So he said, even though I am the author of Jatir Vraniam, I am not the responsible party. And then we have seen that he said the Namaam Karmani limpanti Namay karmafulasproha. Why I am not attached to that? Because I am not Karma Falas proha.
You only get attached when you have Karma falasproha. From the selfs perspective, he does not have anything to gain. So at macro level, the Bhagavan has nothing to achieve and therefore he has no desire.
As long as you have no desire, you cannot be bound by it. At a micro level, all the desires are at my intellectual and mental level only myself is not participating in it. As the self, Im completely detached from my actions.
So the actions are performed at the body level, are taught as the mind level desired at the intellectual and mental level. So these sufferers are also mind, body and intellect only. My actions are not right physical level, I suffer through physical level.
At a mental level, I suffer through mind and suffer through intellect when they are wrong. But the self is not attached. Therefore the Namam Karmani Limpanti self is not affected by any actions, good, bad or ugly.
Just as our analogy of space, the quality of the space inside the room is exactly the same as outside the room. This space, no matter how I try to contaminate it, will not be affected and will not change its characteristics. Because it remains exactly same as the universal space outside.
So myself in me is also in the same manner is not getting affected by my actions. Ithima yo Vijayanarti Karma Vihen NASA badhya. The one who knows this then my accents are only binding my body, mind and intellect.
Therefore the enjoyers and sufferers are nothing but the body, mind and intellect. At the ego level only, the self is not participating and not suffering. One who knows that Karma bhi NASA Badhyate actions do not bind them.
Many people in the past, your ancestors knew this. And they continue to perform actions as required by their duties and the roles theyve taken. But knowing that core of their being is not affected by these actions.
They lived very successful life and liberated themselves. And therefore Im now advising you that you should also do this. Because one thing is clear.
You cannot live without actions. Action is a signature of life. As long as youre alive, you have to perform actions. When actions stop thats your death.
Only in death you will be actionless. Action you must perform. But you need to change the attitude towards action. So you become actionless.
You as the core of your being is not participating in these actions. So you align yourself with the one which is not participating. Not align one which is fighting this battle.
Thats how you will become actionless. Goal is to become liberated from actions. One way to liberate from action is to become actionless.
If I dont drive, Meena and I always argue you have a lot of traffic tickets. Look at me, Ive only got one or two. Compare the amount of miles I drive and compare the mile you drive.
Then put a probability on every hundred thousand miles you drive or 10,000 how many tickets you got and how many tickets I got. So one way to not get a ticket is what? But you can avoid that. Because you cant come from your home to the class without driving.
So driving is unavoidable. So somehow you have to avoid getting tickets of other means. So action is unavoidable in life.
So getting bound by the action is also unavoidable. But there may be other means to not getting attached is not identifying with the one who is acting. Then when you disown your relative who is doing something bad, you are no more attached to the actions.
As long as you are relating to that. I am part of that organization which is doing something wrong. You are bound by that.
You detach yourself from that. You are just a witness now. So there must be another way of detaching ourselves from actions.
Our Sastra says there is a way. The concept Saksi Chaitanya. Just as when I am watching other people witnessing what other people are doing, I am not getting affected.
Because I am just witness. You are doing some two people are fighting. I cannot be blamed for that fight the same.
If I start seeing my actions as a third party then I will not be bound by my actions. Its called Saksichaitanya. So the next verse says Kim Karma Kim Akarma IDHI kavayo ABHI atramo hita ha.
And even in our day to day life we call Kavi a poet as a Kavi in our vernacular languages. But Kavi with the name of a Rishi was a great Rishi who has written so many of these. You know Richas in Vedas.
So after that, even the other Rishis, other people who were wise, were also called Kavis. The word Kavi became a connotation for a very wise person. A wise person is supposed to know what is right and what is wrong.
But he says karmas are so complex that even wise people do not know what is action and what is inaction. They get confused, deluded by that. See, in this world, if we look at the relationship of cause and effect, everything in our universe works on cause and effect.
So this universe is a very predictable universe. There is nothing in this universe which cannot be predicted as long as you know all the factors which are acting on that action. So when you send the Mars, whatever the Yan as long as you calculate all the forces and act on that correctly and perfectly, it will land exactly as you plan.
If you dont know one factor which is affecting it, you will not be able to predict where it is going to land. So if you know everything about how the world reacts to actions, you will be able to predict what the results would be. Not very difficult in theory.
But it is difficult to know how many things will affect my actions in this world. I submit a proposal and I think I have done everything I know. So the result should be this.
What I dont know is what the other people are doing, what their proposals would be like and therefore I cannot predict. Therefore I shouldnt be worried about what will come out of that. Therefore I said the nature of action in action is so complex because so many factors affect the result.
They even get confused when they try to predict what will happen. Tate Karma Pravakshami -- therefore I am going to tell you what Karma is, not what Karma Phala (the fruits of action) will be, but what the nature of action itself is.

These verses address one of the most profound puzzles of spiritual life: Kim karma kim akarma iti kavayo py atra mohitah - even the wise are confused about what is action and what is inaction. Krishna promises to explain this mysterious subject, for understanding it liberates one from all evil. The teaching culminates in verse 18: one who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is the wisest among people, a true yogi who has accomplished all actions (kritsnakarmakrit).
What does it mean to see inaction in action? When you become so skilled at something that your mind and intellect are no longer effortfully engaged, the action becomes automatic - like driving a car after years of practice. The deeper teaching is that the Self is always inactive; only the body, mind, and intellect act. Conversely, apparent inaction can be the most powerful action - like a supervisor whose mere presence makes workers productive, or a political leader whose decision not to act shapes history. By not acting, you are still doing something with consequences.
Today, observe your actions throughout the day. Notice which activities engage your full mental effort and which flow naturally without strain. When driving, walking, or doing routine tasks, recognize that you (the witnessing Self) are not truly acting - it is the conditioned body-mind operating. Also notice where you are not acting - and what effect that inaction is having. Are there good intentions being overwhelmed by neglect? The wise person understands that the nature of action is gahana - deep and mysterious. Results depend on countless factors beyond your knowledge or control. Focus on performing right action with the understanding that the Self is always the non-participant witness (sakshi chaitanya), and you will find freedom even while engaged in intense activity.
